newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Divs qualify as income for NZ pension plan-Peters.
newsitem.headline: Divs qualify as income for NZ pension plan-Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Tuesday that earnings derived from dividends would be considered income for the purposes of the proposed compulsory pension savings scheme. "If your earnings are coming from dividends, then I expect people to save, because there will be a tax cut on that basis," Peters told journalists after addressing the Association of Investment Advisers and Financial Planners.
"If you're making a tax declaration derived from dividend income or other income and you're getting an eight percent equivalent tax cut -- why wouldn't you be saving that?"

In broad terms, the proposed scheme would see everyone in New Zealand contributing a portion of their income to a personal pension saving scheme regulated by the government -- initially three percent in 1998/99, rising to eight percent by 2002.
Peters declined to comment on whether capital gains would also be considered income for the purposes of the savings scheme, however.
He said the tax status of the interest earned in the compulsory funds was being addressed by a design team working on the proposed scheme at the moment.
Peters said he expected the framework of the proposed scheme to be available "sometime after the first of June".
A referendum will be held on the scheme in September.
